turns.content: Planet X and planet Y orbit equal-radius stars. Star Y's photosphere is twice as hot; planet Y is at half the orbital distance and has twice planet X's circumference. Derive how the total stellar power intercepted by a planet depends on stellar luminosity, orbital distance, and planet radius.
Calculate the stellar-luminosity ratio and identify which temperature ratio enters the Stefan-Boltzmann law.
What distance-only dilution factor follows from planet Y being twice as close to its star?
Translate the circumference ratio into the planetary cross-sectional-area factor required by the intercepted-power relation. Does the equal rotation rate affect the instantaneous intercepted power?
Combine the stellar-luminosity, orbital-distance, and planetary-size factors to find the ratio of intercepted power.
Do any other temperature quantity or the equal rotation rates change the intercepted-power comparison? Explain.
Report the intercepted-power ratio and list the physical assumptions used to obtain it.
